candidate.title: smMIP
candidate.scope: Assigned ungrouped smMIP poster row under DNA Low-Level Detection: a genomic target is copied into a degenerately tagged molecular inversion probe circle, selected by exonuclease treatment, amplified into an indexed sequencing library, read and grouped by capture identity to obtain a corrected target sequence. The separate lower MIPSTR row is visible context, with an independent input and horizontal workflow; it is not an alternative branch of the assigned smMIP schematic. Hiatt et al. supports the smMIP implementation used to clarify this row; the record does not assert that every smMIP implementation has identical complete preparation or analysis.

states.label: Degenerately tagged smMIP DNA capture probe
features: Single-stranded probe with two arms complementary to sequences flanking the target and a common backbone.

features: The circle contains newly synthesized sequence complementary to the selected genomic interval, covalently joined to the probe.

This boundary represents the post-capture mixture: residual genomic DNA and uncircularized probes have not yet undergone the following exonuclease selection.

features: Reads are associated with the same sample, probe/target and molecular tag. A tag alone is not treated as globally unique across all samples and targets.

evidence.locator: smMIP arrow into Align fragments from every unique molecular tag; True variant and Random error labels

evidence.quote: Groups of fr-reads assigned to the same probe via alignment to the reference genome and sharing the same molecular tag and sample index form a “tag-defined read group” (TDRG).
Random errors (yellow) that occur during library construction and sequencing may be present in some members of the TDRG at some positions.

states.label: Corrected target sequence / single molecule consensus read
features: Consensus represents the captured genomic target sequence; the shared variant is retained while inconsistent random errors are reduced.
Synthetic targeting-arm bases are excluded from target consensus in the checked smMIP implementation.

Molecule-level target calls support low-frequency variant detection and quantitation across captured molecules. Residual source-DNA damage errors can survive consensus; the depiction does not establish error-free detection or a universal sensitivity threshold.

evidence.locator: smMIP arrow from stacked read family to Corrected sequence; orange shared variant retained

evidence.quote: TDRGs are used to call a single molecule consensus sequence (“smc-read”) for the captured target sequence that is robust to such errors.
Positions expected to be derived from probe targeting arms (and therefore synthetic DNA) were excluded from consideration at this step.
Errors in smc-reads predominantly exhibit patterns consistent with DNA damage, namely, the oxidative adduct 8-oxo-guanine and deamination of cytosine or 5-methyl-cytosine

Single molecule tagging, on the other hand, enables consensus calling for single genomic equivalents present in the input material, thereby facilitating both highly sensitive variant calling and precise quantitation of mutation frequency.

operations.label: Genomic DNA
operations.description: Hybridize the smMIP’s two targeting arms to sequences flanking the selected genomic interval, producing the looped probe–template complex shown under Genomic DNA. The left Gene icon defines the target; it is not treated as a separate preparation step.
operations.mechanism: Complementary target-flanking arms bind genomic DNA while leaving a gap over the sequence to be copied.
operations.information_effect: The probe selects a genomic interval and brings its pre-existing molecular tag to that capture event.

operations.label: Copy target sequence
operations.description: Copy the intervening genomic target into the bound probe and close it into a tagged single-stranded circle; the original genomic DNA is still present at this boundary.
operations.mechanism: Polymerase gap filling synthesizes the reverse complement of the genomic target; ligase joins the probe into a single-stranded circle.
operations.information_effect: The newly synthesized target copy becomes physically linked to a molecular tag before amplification.

operations.label: Exonuclease
operations.description: Degrade uncircularized probes and genomic DNA after target copying, leaving tagged capture circles as amplification substrates. The faded diagram elements are interpreted using the paper’s explicit substrate statement.
operations.mechanism: Exonuclease treatment removes uncircularized DNA; the figure does not depict a new tag or target-copying event here.
operations.information_effect: Enriches surviving circular capture products without establishing perfect biological specificity.

operations.information_effect: Groups repeated observations of a captured progenitor sequence, preserving sample identity and locus context for consensus.
